checks.claim: Gateway is healthy before recovery operations.
Identity service is healthy before recovery operations.
User service is healthy before recovery operations.
A synthetic identity account is persisted in PostgreSQL.
A synthetic user record is persisted in PostgreSQL.
The synthetic account refresh-token hash metadata is persisted in PostgreSQL.
Authoritative synthetic records survive a PostgreSQL container restart.
Protected reads remain correct after core application service restarts.
The user-list Redis cache is populated from a protected read.
The disposable Redis cache can be cleared independently of PostgreSQL.
A protected read still succeeds after Redis is cleared.
The user-list cache is reconstructed after an authoritative read.
A non-empty PostgreSQL custom-format backup is created.
A SHA-256 checksum and byte size are recorded for the backup without publishing the backup itself.
A fresh isolated PostgreSQL recovery database is created without replacing the primary database.
The PostgreSQL backup restores successfully into the fresh recovery database.
The identity record in the recovered database exactly matches its baseline snapshot.
The user record in the recovered database exactly matches its baseline snapshot.
Refresh-token metadata in the recovered database exactly matches its baseline snapshot.
An isolated identity-service instance backed by the recovered database authenticates the restored identity.
An isolated user-service instance backed by the recovered database reads the restored user.
The pre-backup refresh credential is accepted by the identity service backed by the recovered database.
The primary gateway path remains operational after isolated recovery validation.
